Never trust the subscription number. This IPO lost almost all its listing gain.
Four mainboard IPOs listed in the first week of November.
Most people think more subscription means bigger gains. So here's the scoreboard. Issue price, listing day, and today.
But wait. The least wanted IPO of the four is now beating the sixty four times one.
B L S Polymers. Two hundred forty one times subscribed. Up seventy nine percent on day one, and eighty four percent by Tuesday.
S F C Environmental. Only nine and a half times subscribed, yet it hit the upper circuit on day one. Now up thirty one percent.

Bombay Coated. Sixty four times subscribed, up sixteen percent on day one. Then three lower circuits in a row. Now just one point seven percent up. And M K Sons? Five times subscribed, flat on day one, now up sixteen.
So here's the answer. Subscription shows demand on bidding day, not where the price goes next. Listing day is one chapter, not the whole story.
